author: Chris Hammill <cfhammill@gmail.com>
message:
Fix slice matrix dimensions in plot.antsImage

In situations where:

```
winrows <- round(length(slices) / ncolumns) ## rounding down
wincols <- round(length(slices) / winrows)    ## rounding down
```

the product of winrows and wincols can be less than length(slices) causing an error.

Ex:

```
img <- makeImage(c(10,10,10), array(1:1000, dim = c(10,10,10)))
plot.antsImage(img, ncolumns = 4, slice = 1:9)
```

New code honours the user specified ncolumns ```wincols <- ncolumns``` and uses ceiling to compute the number of
rows, this ensures sufficient space.

author: Shrinidhi KL <nidhi84shri@gmail.com>
message:
* The programs( which take name=value args ) can now take arguments in both the following forms:
** program-name( <comma-separated-list-of-arguments> )
eg: antsMotionCorr( "-d" , 3 , "-o" , "[" , "foo" , moco_img , avg_img , "]" , "-m" , "MI[" , avg_img , img , 1 , 32 , 50 , "]" , "-t" , "Rigid[0.01]" , "-i" , 25 , "-u" , 1 , "-e" , 1 , "-s" , 0 , "-f" , 1 , "-n" , 25 )
** program-name( <named-list-of-arguments> )
eg: antsMotionCorr( list( d = 3 , o = list( moco_params , moco_img , avg_img ) , m = list( name = "MI" , avg_img , img , 1 , 32 , 50 ) , t = "Rigid[0.01]" , i = 25 , u = 1 , e = 1 , s = 0 , f = 1 , n = 25 ) )
The second form is better and makes more sense.
* The programs can now accept and return multiple images.
Example is in the following script for 'Atropos'.
* The programs can now return data directly to R instead of writing csv files.
Example is in the following script for 'antsMotionCorr'.

The following script gives an example using the above changes:
library(ANTsR)
img = antsImageRead( "KKI2009-01-fMRI.nii" , "float" , 4 )
avg_img = new( "antsImage" , "float" , 3 )
antsMotionCorr( list( d = 3 , a = img , o = avg_img ) )
moco_img = new( "antsImage" , "float" , 4 )
moco_params = new( "antsMatrix" , "double" )
antsMotionCorr( list( d = 3 , o = list( moco_params , moco_img , avg_img ) , m = list( name = "MI" , avg_img , img , 1 , 32 , 50 ) , t = "Rigid[0.01]" , i = 25 , u = 1 , e = 1 , s = 0 , f = 1 , n = 25 ) )
bm_img = new( "antsImage" , "float" , 3 )
ThresholdImage( 3 , avg_img , bm_img , "Otsu" , 3 )
ThresholdImage( 3 , bm_img , bm_img , 2 , 3 )
ImageMath( 3 , bm_img , "ME" , bm_img , 1 )
ImageMath( 3 , bm_img , "GetLargestComponent" , bm_img )
ImageMath( 3 , bm_img , "MD" , bm_img , 1 )
ImageMath( 3 , bm_img , "ME" , bm_img , 1 )
compcorr_corr_img = new( "antsImage" , "float" , 4 )
compcorr_var_img = new( "antsImage" , "float" , 3 )
ImageMath( 4 , antsImagePair( compcorr_corr_img , compcorr_var_img ) , "CompCorrAuto" , moco_img , bm_img , 6 )
N3BiasFieldCorrection( 3 , avg_img , avg_img , 2 , bm_img )
N3BiasFieldCorrection( 3 , avg_img , avg_img , 1 , bm_img )
N3BiasFieldCorrection( 3 , avg_img , avg_img , 1 , bm_img )
N3BiasFieldCorrection( 3 , avg_img , avg_img , 1 , bm_img )
bm_img_uint = antsImageClone( bm_img , "unsigned int" )
seg_img_uint = new( "antsImage" , "unsigned int" , 3 )
Atropos( list( d = 3 , a = avg_img , a = compcorr_var_img , m = "[0.3,1x1x1]" , o = seg_img_uint , c = "[5,0]" , i = "kmeans[3]" , x = bm_img_uint ) )
prob_img_list = new( "antsImageList" , "float" , 3 )
Atropos( list( d = 3 , a = avg_img , a = compcorr_var_img , m = "[0.3,1x1x1]" , o = list( seg_img_uint , prob_img_list ) , c = "[5,0]" , i = "kmeans[3]" , x = bm_img_uint ) )
Atropos( list( d = 3 , a = avg_img , a = compcorr_var_img , m = "[0.3,1x1x1]" , o = list( seg_img_uint , prob_img_list ) , c = "[5,0]" , i = list( name = "priorprobabilityimages" , 3 , prob_img_list , 0 ) , x = bm_img_uint ) )
seg_img_float = antsImageClone( seg_img_uint , "float" )
cortmask_img = new( "antsImage" , "float" , 3 )
ThresholdImage( 3 , seg_img_float , cortmask_img , 2 , 2 )
cortmask_img_double = antsImageClone( cortmask_img , "double" )
moco_img_double = antsImageClone( moco_img , "double" )
mat = new( "antsMatrix" , "double" )
sccan( list( "timeseriesimage-to-matrix" = list( moco_img_double , cortmask_img_double , 0.0 , 0.0  ) , o = mat ) )

The output 'moco_params' of program 'antsMotionCorr' is available in R as an object that can be converted to a list or a data-frame:
moco_params_df = as.data.frame( moco_params )
moco_params_lst = as.list( moco_params )
From a list or data.frame, R provides a lot of functions to convert to other type of R objects. We can manipulate those objects and convert them back to 'antsMatrix' as follows.
mod_moco_params_df = as.data.frame( <modified moco-params in some R object> )
moco_params = as.antsMatrix( mod_moco_params_df )
mod_moco_params_lst = as.list( <modified moco-params in some R object> )
moco_params = as.antsMatrix( mod_moco_params_lst )
Same is true with the output 'mat' of 'sccan' above. The data is available as a list or data-frame and can be converted and manipulated and converted back to 'antsMatrix', which can then be fed to other programs.

for the labels and recompute the final label set in order to correctly derive the output
segmentation map.  this is a BUG that should be addressed in the future.  the second
issue is that this function creates a side effect of modifying the input mask such that
only non-zero label regions are passed to JLF at the c++ level.

author: Shrinidhi KL <nidhi84shri@gmail.com>
message:
Following features added to the package:

* Convert an 'antsImage' into a vector/matrix/array
vect = as.numeric( img [ , mask = <> ] [ , region = <> ] )
vect = as.matrix( img [ , mask = <> ] [ , region = <> ] )
vect = as.array( img [ , mask = <> ] [ , region = <> ] )
img -- input image of class 'antsImage' ;
mask -- logical vector/matrix/array ; default = logical() ( effectively no mask ) ;
length of mask can either number-of-pixels in the region considered or number-of-pixels in one slice of the region considered where 'slice' represents the last dimension in the region ; in the case where mask is for a slice, the mask is replicated for to match the length of the region
region -- image region to consider for conversion ; default = img->LargestPossibleRegion() ( entire input image ) ;
any valid region for the image
vect -- vector/matrix/array with dimensions equal to dimensions of the region considered ;

* Convert a matrix/array into an 'antsImage'
img = as.antsImage( vect [ , pixeltype = <> ] [ , spacing = <> ] [ , origin = <> ]  )
vect -- matrix/array of dimensions 2,3 or 4
pixeltype -- pixeltype of the result image; default = "double"
spacing -- spacing of the result image ; default = as.numeric( <vector of 1s of length = dimensions(vect)> )
origin -- origin of the result image ; default = as.numeric( <vector of 0s of length = dimensions(vect)> )
img -- image of class 'antsImage' with dimensions = dimensions(vect), spacing and origin as provided or defaults

* Index into an 'antsImage' using '[]' operator for reading
vect = img[ mask ]
vect = img[ list( mask = <> , region = <> ) ]
vect = img[ mask , region ]
img, mask, region, vect -- same as above
vect = img[ row , col [, slice] [, time] ]
number of indices should match image dimensions; use 'NULL' or 'integer(0)' to access whole dimension
vect -- vector of pixel-values with 'row' as a fastest moving dimension

* Index into an 'antsImage' using '[]' operator for writing
img[ mask ] = value
img[ list( mask = <> , region = <> ) ] = value
img[ mask , region ] = value
img, mask, region -- same as above
value -- vector/matrix/array of length equal to number-of-pixels in the region considered
img[ row , col [, slice] [, time] ] = vect
vect -- same as for accessor case

* Relational operators( == , != , <= , >= , < , > )
vect = ( img == value )
vect = ( img == list( value = <> , region = <> ) )
value -- numeric scalar that is to be compared with every pixel in the region
region -- 'antsRegion' to use for comparison
vect -- logical vector with dimensions equal to dimensions of the region considered
